content.user_title: Analyze Binaries With Reverse Engineering Workflows
content.value_statement: Binary analysis can be slow when the workflow is unclear. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured reverse engineering guidance.
actual_capabilities: Plans authorized static and dynamic binary analysis workflows.
Explains how to identify file type, architecture, imports, exports, and entry points.
Guides use of IDA Pro, Ghidra, radare2, x64dbg, GDB, and related tools.
Helps document functions, data structures, algorithms, and security findings.
Recognizes common patterns such as XOR strings, anti-debugging checks, API hashing, and stack strings.
limitations: Requires authorized samples, binaries, or analysis context from the user.
Does not include bundled reverse engineering tools or runnable scripts.
Cannot guarantee decompiler accuracy for obfuscated, packed, or damaged binaries.
Should not be used for unauthorized access, malware creation, license bypass, or intellectual property theft.

use_cases.title: Triage Unknown Binaries
use_cases.description: Build a first-pass analysis plan for file type, architecture, imports, strings, and likely protections.

use_cases.title: Solve CTF Challenges
use_cases.description: Create a structured path from binary identification to comparison breakpoints and validation logic review.

use_cases.title: Document Closed-Source Libraries
use_cases.description: Map exported functions, authentication flows, data structures, and runtime behavior for authorized interoperability work.

prompt_templates.title: Start Binary Triage
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me triage this authorized binary. Ask for any missing details, then outline the first static analysis steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Decompiler Review
prompt_templates.prompt: I loaded an authorized sample in Ghidra or IDA. Help me identify entry points, important functions, and useful renames.

prompt_templates.title: Design Dynamic Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a safe dynamic analysis plan for this authorized binary. Include breakpoints, monitoring points, and expected evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Produce Findings Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn my authorized reverse engineering notes into a concise report. Cover behavior, data structures, risks, and verification steps.

output_examples.input: I have an authorized CTF binary that asks for a password.
output_examples.output: The response outlines file identification, protection checks, decompiler review, comparison breakpoints, and evidence to record.

output_examples.input: I need to understand an authorized DLL authentication flow.
output_examples.output: The response suggests export review, function naming, controlled runtime tracing, parameter capture, and documentation of security assumptions.

output_examples.input: I found obfuscated strings in a sample.
output_examples.output: The response explains how to locate decode routines, identify keys, validate recovered strings, and document the algorithm.

best_practices: Confirm authorization and scope before analyzing any binary.
Work in an isolated environment when dynamic analysis may execute unknown code.
Record evidence, tool versions, assumptions, and verification steps in the final notes.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill to bypass licensing or access controls illegally.
Do not execute unknown binaries on a normal workstation.
Do not trust decompiler output without checking assembly and runtime evidence.

faq.question: What tools does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It references IDA Pro, Ghidra, radare2, x64dbg, GDB, Frida, pwntools, Capstone, Unicorn, angr, and related workflows.

faq.question: Can it analyze malware?
faq.answer: It can guide defensive malware analysis when the user has authorization and uses an isolated environment.

faq.question: Does it run analysis tools for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides methods, checklists, and interpretation guidance. Users must run tools in their own safe environment.

faq.question: Is it suitable for CTF work?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes CTF-oriented triage, password-check analysis, breakpoint planning, and validation review.

faq.question: Can it help with closed-source software?
faq.answer: Yes, when the work is authorized, such as interoperability, security review, or internal software assessment.

faq.question: What safety rules does it include?
faq.answer: It directs users toward authorized research and rejects unauthorized access, malicious malware creation, license bypass, theft, and illegal activity.
